claim: Three texts, six instruments, one method on all three islands.

paras: Before going on site, each group read one text on public life and turned it into two field instruments, called toolkits. Every group then used all six, the same way, in its own area. We surveyed each island on two days, one weekday and one rest day, each in three blocks: 10:00 to 12:00, 16:00 to 18:00 and 20:00 to 22:00. Because the method is the same, the three islands can be set side by side.

cols.source: Public Spaces and Public Life: Perth 2009
cols.author: Gehl Architects, 2009

kits.title: Land use and building scale
kits.text: What each street face is made of: storeys, uses, doors and blank wall, graded A (active) to E (inactive).

kits.title: Activity, comfort and safety
kits.text: What people do when they stop in the street, and what lets them stay.

cols.source: Soft City: Building Density for Everyday Life
cols.author: David Sim, 2019

kits.title: Density and housing quality
kits.text: How densely each plot is built and lived in, beside a housing quality score out of 32.

kits.title: Layering vs stacking
kits.text: Whether a building changes from front to back and from ground to roof, or repeats one floor.

kits.title: Walking activity and movement count
kits.text: Everyone passing a line across the street in ten minutes, tallied in shade or in sun.

kits.title: Public space quality and microclimate
kits.text: Thirteen qualities of each public space, from safety to shade, scored 1 to 5.
